attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post. It is a factual premise inside his parenthetical aside, not a quotation of anyone else.

semantics.note: The embedded premise is a firm factual assertion about what had been published as of 2023-03-29. The normalisation matches it, with no added scope.

contract.note: The plain reading counts substantive specifics (size, compute, data makeup) as 'details'. This is the ordinary reading in context, since he was asking how anyone could compare power to GPT-4. It matches OpenAI's own 'no further details' framing. It is neither stretched for nor against him.

evidence.note: The primary report, dated 2023-03-14, is direct evidence of what was published. It states that it withholds architecture (including model size), compute, and dataset construction.

The same passage gives generic labels: Transformer-style, public plus licensed data, RLHF. Under the plain reading these are not substantive details, so they do not contradict the claim. They would only undercut a strictly literal reading.
The arXiv v1 abstract (2023-03-15) gives only a generic architecture label. It confirms the date and how little was disclosed.

reviews.rationale: The GPT-4 technical report, published before the post, explicitly withheld model size, architecture, compute, and dataset construction. Its only disclosures were generic labels. On the fair plain reading this supports the claim. A strictly literal 'no details' would be overstated, because generic facts were given. The packet did not check informal disclosures beyond the report.
